sections.title: Complex scalars, vectors, and conjugation

sections.worked_case: z=2-3i,w=-1+4i; v=(1+i,2-i) with squared length7, scaling by i and2-i, and normalization.

sections.title: Inner products, adjoints, and orthogonality

sections.entry: 2.1 complex coordinate arithmetic and conjugation; all inner-product, norm and local array notation defined here.
sections.exit: Derive Cauchy–Schwarz including equality/zero cases, construct a unique nearest projection, and distinguish conjugation, transpose and adjoint.
sections.worked_case: a=(1,i), v=(2,1+i), overlap3-i, projection/residual squared lengths5/1; explicit2-by-2 adjoint identity.
sections.boundary: Positive-definite inner products; standard-coordinate matrix bridge defined locally, full linear-map/basis theory owned by2.3. Projection is not a measurement postulate.
sections.code_plan: Complete examples/foundations/inner_products.py: PyTorch2.13.0 CPU complex128 versus independent real/imaginary integer arithmetic; no FlagQuantum required.
sections.independent_check: 81 vectors/6561 ordered inner products; hand-computed half-integer projection, adjoint common scalar2-6i, non-real scaling, dot/conjugation error counterexamples, zero/equality cases.
sections.transfer_task: Reverse projection overlap, omit denominator, diagnose missing positive definiteness, rescale direction; accessible full answers.

sections.title: Linear maps, bases, and changes of coordinates

sections.boundary: Finite-dimensional linear maps; no determinant/eigenvalue machinery or physical-gate interpretation. Unitary criterion introduced locally, broader operator properties owned by2.4.

sections.title: Hermitian, unitary, and positive operators

sections.entry: 2.3 linear maps and coordinate representations, with2.2 adjoint identity; eigenpair and positive form notation defined locally.
sections.exit: Prove real Hermitian eigenvalues, positivity from real nonnegative quadratic forms, and unitary norm preservation; distinguish the classes with counterexamples.
sections.worked_case: Complex Hermitian H=[[2,i],[-i,2]], diagonal unitary U=diag(1,i), indefinite Z and semidefinite projector P; non-Hermitian nilpotent counterexample.
sections.boundary: Finite-dimensional operators in orthonormal coordinates; no spectral decomposition imported from2.5. Positivity proof uses quadratic forms and entry probes, not sampled certification.
sections.code_plan: CPU complex128 PyTorch checks versus scalar real/imaginary form and hand-supplied eigenpairs; no FlagQuantum needed.
sections.independent_check: Expanded positive quadratic form, eigenpair residuals, norm identities and explicit failed Hermitian/unitary/positive implications.

sections.boundary: Finite Hermitian theorem and arbitrary rectangular complex SVD; no general normal spectral theorem or polar decomposition required. Real completeness used in the local compactness lemma.

sections.entry: 2.5 spectral projectors and decomposition; scalar exponential and absolute-convergence bridges supplied locally without assuming operator norms.
